dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Kamila, I'm going home to Aktobe for Nauryz next week. What do you usually do for the holiday in your family?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Oh, Nauryz is my favourite time of year! My family has a lot of traditions. We always start early in the morning. My mother and grandmother begin cooking the night before.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Do you still make Nauryz kozhe at home? My grandmother used to make it with fresh milk from the farm. But in the city, we buy everything from a shop now.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Yes, we always make it ourselves! My grandmother knows the traditional recipe by heart. She never uses a written recipe — it's all in her memory. She used to cook it in a huge outdoor cauldron when she was young.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: That sounds amazing. In my family, we used to have a big yurt in the garden for Nauryz. All the relatives would come — maybe fifty or sixty people! But my grandfather passed away three years ago, and now we celebrate more quietly.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That must have been a wonderful tradition. My family didn't use to have a yurt, but we always set up long tables outside. The whole street used to come! It was so loud and joyful.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Do you play any traditional games? My cousins and I used to run races in the yard. The winner got a special prize from Grandfather — usually a beautiful scarf or a book.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: We play a game called 'Altybakan' — a big swing that families build together. Young people sing songs while swinging. It's a really old tradition. My grandmother says she played it as a child.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I've never heard of Altybakan! It sounds wonderful. I think modern Nauryz is quite different from how it used to be. There are more concerts and shopping now — less of the simple, community spirit.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I agree. But the most important thing hasn't changed — it's still about being together, forgiveness, and a fresh start. Those values will never go out of fashion.
